children: German state railway company Deutsche Bahn's loss-making freight division DB Cargo no longer expects to make a profit this year, it said on Thursday, after booking a €260 million ($298.5 million) writedown from its British subsidiary that it expects to sell.
DB Cargo says the writedown needed to be booked this year as binding offers are expected shortly.
It said that its German turnaround remains on track, with first-half earnings improving by more than €100 million, including €87 million from operating performance.
EU rules require DB Cargo to become profitable by the end of 2026.

Chief Executive Bernhard Osburg said the company needs more time to complete its restructuring, with the goal of making it "operate as an integrated, competitive, and sustainable profitable European rail logistics provider" by 2031.
DB Cargo aims to sell its British subsidiary by the end of 2026.
